title: Category-need evidence anchor cited in-repo (M0)
context: PLAN v0.2 adds an M0 requirement: the category-need evidence base must be cited in-repo so cold-start work has an evidentiary anchor independent of a named partner. The evidence includes: (1) ad-hoc/family/child-interpreter harm vs. professional interpreters (Flores et al.; AHRQ PSNet 'language barrier'); (2) legal duty under Title VI / ACA §1557 (2024 final rule) to provide qualified interpreters; (3) Google-Translate ED-discharge accuracy study (*J. Emergency Medicine*, 2025) showing ~67% Farsi and ~55% Armenian accuracy, and the ATA conclusion that MT is not adequate for medical instructions. This same evidence is the core argument for why the project exists and why raw MT/LLM output is never shipped for high-tier phrases.
objective: Write and commit an in-repo evidence-anchor document citing the key category-need studies, legal duties, and competitive baseline findings that justify the project's existence and review discipline.
acceptanceCriteria: Documents cite ad-hoc/family/child-interpreter harm evidence (Flores et al.; AHRQ PSNet) with correct attribution
Cites ACA §1557 (2024 final rule) and Title VI qualified-interpreter duty (HHS OCR; National Health Law Program) with source URLs and access dates

Cites the Google-Translate ED-discharge accuracy study (J. Emergency Medicine 2025) and ATA analysis, stating the language-accuracy ranges (>90% Spanish, ~67% Farsi, ~55% Armenian) and the conclusion that MT is not adequate for emergency medical instructions
States explicitly why the same suspicion applies to LLM output and why this project uses reviewed translation not MT/LLM-only
Committed in-repo with verifiable source URLs and access dates; references marked as 'verify current terms per source' where terms may change
Links from PLAN.md References section (already present in v0.2)
